To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nitrogen adsorbed in grooves of bundles of single-walled closed-cap carbon nanotubes exhibits a linear dependence of its heat capacity on temperature in the region 1–3 K, while in the region 3–8 K its heat capacity follows the Debye law with T3 dependence.

the heat capacity of bundles containing one-dimensional chains of N2 molecules adsorbed into the grooves of the bundles has been first studied experimentally at temperatures from 5 to 40  K using an adi adic calorimeter.
nitrogen chain in grooved bundles of closed-cap carbon nanotubes has been first experimentallly studied at temperatures from T = 2 to T = 40 K.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the experimental investigation of the heat capacity of nitrogen molecules in the grooves between the single-walled carbon-nanotube bundles.
the study of the heat capacity of the N2 chains adsorbed in grooves of bundles of closed cap single walled carbon nanotubs.
the heat capacity of nitrogen CN2 in the grooves in bundles of closed-cap nanotubes at temperatures from 0.7 to 40  K.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the heat capacity of nitrogen in grooves of bundles of closed cap SWNTs has a pronounced one-dimensional character in the region 2 to 8 K and is determined by the vibrational degrees of freedom of nitrogen molecules.
the heat capacity of the nitrogen chain in groves of single-walled nanotube bundles is a combination of the phonon and rotational heat capacities of the N2 molecule.

the heat capacity of the 1D chain of N2 molecules in the grooves is a combination of the contributions from the phonon modes of the chain and rotational modes of the molecules, and the contribution from the rotational modes dominates at temperatures above 8 K.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the experimental heat capacities of nitrogen in the grooves can be described by the Debye model with a Debye temperature of 30.6 K.

the heat capacity of N2 chains in grooves of SWCNT bundles has been studied at the temperature range from 2 to T > 40 K, and the contribution of the N2 chains to the total heat capacities was separated.
nitrogen molecules are more mobile in the SWNT grooves than krypton atoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat capacity of the nitrogen chain is significantly lower than that of the Kr chain.
nitrogen chains are more sensitive to the interaction with the SWCNT walls than the Kr chains, which is in agreement with the results of our previous work.
the heat capacity of nitrogen molecules in grooves of SWCNT bundles can be used to study the rotational degrees of the freedom of the molecules.
